## Purpose

A `*_state` module in `shared/` answers one narrow, measured question about the repository or working tree — `branch_state` classifies which work-unit branches exist and what state each is in; `code_state` fingerprints the working tree to tell a fresh test run from a stale one. Both stay pure readers: they take a `Path`/callback and return plain data, never a handle capable of acting on the repository. Both document, in the module doc-comment, exactly what is measured and what is deliberately NOT (a stated boundary, not an assumed one).

## Convention

Folder: apps/rt/src/shared/** · Extension: .rs · Files of this role in this subproject: 2

Both exemplars are read-only and structurally cannot mutate: `code_state::fingerprint` never writes, and `branch_state`'s own doc states "the module cannot delete anything" as a checked invariant. A `GitOut`-style callback type (`type GitOut<'a> = &'a dyn Fn(&[&str]) -> Option<String>`) is used instead of importing a `commands`-face git primitive directly, because `shared` is a leaf module `hooks`/`commands` may depend on but never the reverse. An answer that "cannot be measured" (no repo, no git, IO error) is `None`, and every caller must read `None` as the FAIL-safe direction for the check (`code_state`: `None` means stale/re-run; `branch_state`: an unmeasured PR is `Unknown`, never a negative).

## How to apply

Name the module `<subject>_state.rs` under `shared/`. State the coverage boundary in the module doc (a table like `code_state`'s "Covered / Not covered" is the expected shape). Take git access as an injected callback or a `Path`, never import a `commands`-face runner. Return plain, cloneable data types with no `Path`/process handle, so a consumer holding the result is provably unable to act on the repository.

## Examples

Ref: apps/rt/src/shared/code_state.rs
Ref: apps/rt/src/shared/branch_state.rs

```rust
/// `true` when a run recorded under `recorded` still describes the tree at
/// `cwd`. An absent recorded fingerprint, or one that cannot be taken now,
/// answers `false` — see [`fingerprint`] on why *cannot tell* is stale.
#[must_use]
pub fn still_current(cwd: &Path, recorded: Option<&str>) -> bool {
    let Some(recorded) = recorded.filter(|s| !s.trim().is_empty()) else {
        return false;
    };
    fingerprint(cwd).is_some_and(|now| now == recorded)
}
```
